decisions.reason: As a modular product line with several models and strong fit to our established camera capabilities, Product B likely meets aspirations sufficiently and, with current growth and organisational slack, should be retained.

Product C extends our existing sensing competences into a related market and, absent clear evidence of performance below aspiration, boundedly rational management would continue it rather than redeploy resources now.

Product D still carries elevated review risk because commercialization signals remain weaker, but its close alignment with our miniaturization strategy and available R&D slack make continued retention more likely than withdrawal.

As a newly launched radiation-hard camera line with a dedicated market presentation and clear fit with our heritage, Product E is unlikely to be dropped within a year unless early results fall well short of aspiration.

Product F is more niche and only tentatively presented, yet it builds on core navigation and imaging know-how, so management would likely tolerate current uncertainty and keep it while monitoring whether results approach aspiration.
